baseline: Existing Python helper, protocol 1, and deployed HighlightBridge; no dependency additions.

coverage.reason: No QML or browser controls change.
Clock calibration is transient; SQLite schema and saved clips stay unchanged.
Existing origin allowlist and native host permissions remain; document checks preserve current session ownership.
Browser presentation timestamps must be translated only within the accepted document origin.
The existing native Python helper has a longer lifetime than game documents.
No user interface or input behavior changes.
Consecutive document and late ping regressions must cross the helper message handler.
WPT demonstrates distinct time origins for contexts created at different times.

behavior.behavior: Contexts created after a delay have different time origins, requiring translation before comparing relative timestamps.
behavior.do_not_copy: Do not copy the browser harness or replace the existing native messaging protocol.

platform.requirement: performance.now is relative to the relevant global time origin; independently created contexts cannot share an unadjusted offset.

proof: node --test test/scripts/highlightsPipeline.test.mjs exercises two documents separated by twelve simulated hours and verifies automatic clip publication.
node --test test/scripts/highlightsProtocol.test.mjs test/scripts/highlightsRepair.test.mjs preserves native message validation and lifecycle handling.
Compare installed helper module hashes with tested source and query status after an idle helper restart.

selection: Reset and seed calibration from accepted session-start before early markers; only the active document can refresh it; discard expired samples. Keep the existing dependency and capture stack.
